analysis_claims.universe: All eligible households; each item's distribution uses its own valid 1–5 responses. Rounded transcription of supplied analysis tables; A2 retains its original wording and coding.
analysis_claims.weighting: wt_final; fixed synthetic target profile; valid-case percentages.

analysis_claims.universe: Each state requires both defining attitudes valid and both agreeing for membership. Joint membership requires all three flags valid. Unknown states are not absence of need.
analysis_claims.weighting: wt_final; original fixed-profile weights. Joint summaries sum supplied unrounded membership percentages.

analysis_claims.universe: Current use: valid U1 among all eligible households. Satisfaction and sharing: valid follow-up answers among recorded current users only. U1 DK/refusal split is unavailable in supplied tables.
analysis_claims.weighting: wt_final; fixed synthetic target profile; separate valid-case denominators for U1, U2 and U3.

findings.proposition: Prioritise a small pilot around quick meals and flexible replanning, with use-up and budget help as closely related tasks. Requests are 60.82%, 59.16% and 57.12%, respectively; sharing attracts 47.23%. These identify a task shortlist, not a statistically established winner.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive evidence supporting a pilot recommendation
findings.qualification: All-household eligible N/weighted N=2700/2700; answered n/weighted n/ESS=2596/2595.96/2045.54 for every item. DK=80, refusal=24; 116 all-zero None respondents remain included. No structural omissions. Multiple-response respondent incidence, not shares of mentions. The three leading tasks differ by at most 3.70 percentage points, below the 8-point attention threshold; no paired superiority test is supplied. Task requests do not establish demand for a digital product.

findings.proposition: Recruit households meeting the effort criteria as a priority pilot audience: they report 2.19 versus 0.97 top-up days per week, a +1.22-day difference (95% CI 1.10 to 1.34; Holm p=3.72e-84), and 3.73 versus 4.93 planned days, a −1.20-day difference (CI −1.36 to −1.04; Holm p=3.28e-48). Both exceed the 0.5-day attention threshold.
findings.qualification: Group order is criteria met/not met. Eligible N/weighted N: 904/809.73 and 1642/1729.28. Top-ups valid n/weighted n/ESS: 878/782.55/661.07 and 1588/1669.18/1286.98; DK/refusal: 18/8 and 42/12. Planning: 872/779.09/656.41 and 1586/1666.86/1285.52; DK/refusal: 22/10 and 40/16. Excluded unknown effort state=154; structural omissions=0. Associations with external reported behaviour do not show that support will reduce these problems or that this audience is commercially superior.

findings.proposition: Include budget and waste needs in the pilot rather than treating effort as the only opportunity. Budget-state households report overspending in at least one of four weeks at 72.31% versus 35.03%: +37.28 points (95% CI 32.70 to 41.86; Holm p=9.69e-57). Waste-state households report 1.87 versus 0.87 discard days per week: +1.00 day (CI 0.87 to 1.14; Holm p=1.04e-47). Both exceed their attention thresholds.
findings.qualification: Budget met/not-met eligible N/weighted N=717/667.29 and 1840/1896.95; valid n/weighted n/ESS=678/631.58/522.17 and 1708/1769.77/1368.26; DK/refusal=33/6 and 107/25; unknown state=143. Waste eligible bases=821/775.51 and 1728/1785.80; valid bases=797/754.72/615.00 and 1664/1721.13/1331.13; DK/refusal=14/10 and 41/23; unknown state=151. Structural omissions=0. Overspending measures incidence, not money; discard measures days, not food quantity. These are separate within-state contrasts, not comparisons between independent need segments.

findings.proposition: Recruit overlapping needs rather than exclusive personas. Effort, waste and budget criteria are met by 31.89%, 30.28% and 26.02% of their respective derivable bases. Among households with all flags valid, 58.89% meet at least one state, 24.44% meet at least two, and 5.93% meet all three.
findings.qualification: Full bases, unknown counts and all eight combinations are retained in analysis_claims.need_state_sizes_and_joint_membership. Joint valid n/weighted n/ESS=2280/2290.14/1799.62, with 420 households lacking at least one flag. Marginal prevalence uses different valid denominators. Numerical prevalence differences do not establish superiority; meeting no defined state does not mean having no support needs.

findings.proposition: Include households with children under 16 as a practical recruitment context. They report 1.91 versus 1.17 top-up days: +0.73 day (95% CI 0.63 to 0.84; Holm p=3.91e-40), exceeding the attention threshold. Their planning difference is smaller: 4.23 versus 4.64 days, −0.40 day (CI −0.54 to −0.27; Holm p=6.64e-9), statistically detectable but below the 0.5-day point-estimate threshold.
findings.qualification: Children/no-children eligible N/weighted N=1296/702 and 1404/1998. Top-ups valid n/weighted n/ESS=1258/681.17/1216.30 and 1356/1926.49/1273.98; DK/refusal=29/9 and 36/12. Planning valid bases=1254/679.47/1212.62 and 1355/1923.93/1272.60; DK/refusal=30/12 and 35/14. No unknown children status or structural omissions. Planning's interval includes differences exceeding 0.5 day in magnitude. Children status is neither a need definition nor a causal explanation.

findings.proposition: Keep participation optional and test delivery format: willingness to welcome digital help is polarised, with 46.82% agreeing, 47.38% disagreeing and only 5.80% neutral. Strong agreement and strong disagreement are each about 35%; a near-midpoint mean would obscure this split.
findings.qualification: Eligible N/weighted N=2700/2700; valid n/weighted n/ESS=2610/2609.19/2057.46; DK=67, refusal=23, structural omissions=0. Full five-category distribution appears in analysis_claims.ordinal_distributions. This is a general attitude, not a tested PantryWorks concept, uptake forecast or evidence that one side exceeds the other.

findings.proposition: Existing tools provide useful comparison experiences, but the study does not establish a dissatisfied replacement market. Current use is 38.90% among valid household screeners. Among valid current-user follow-ups, 83.15% are satisfied and 54.27% have used sharing.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive prevalence and conditional user experience
findings.qualification: Routing, full satisfaction distribution and eligible/valid weighted and unweighted bases with ESS are retained in analysis_claims.tool_routing_and_satisfaction. Satisfaction and sharing percentages apply only to answering current users, not all households. Follow-ups are unasked for 1595 known nonusers and 65 unknown screeners; the latter's DK/refusal split is unavailable. Current users are selected, and satisfaction does not establish tool effectiveness. Older paid-user satisfaction is suppressed: eligible N/weighted N=20/20.36; valid n/weighted n/ESS=18/18.27/17.73; DK=2, refusal=0.

findings.proposition: Test flexibility, low setup effort, acceptable cost and information-sharing controls together. Reported barriers are tightly grouped: rigidity 49.56%, extra cost 49.56%, privacy 48.72% and setup/upkeep 47.90%. Before choosing a format, compare realistic delivery alternatives on task completion and burden; before commercial claims, obtain price evidence, observed uptake, repeated use and controlled outcome evidence.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive barriers and evidence-informed research recommendation
findings.qualification: Barriers eligible N/weighted N=2700/2700; answered n/weighted n/ESS=2570/2574.37/2029.07 for every item; DK=101, refusal=29, structural omissions=0. Includes 204 None respondents. Multiple selections are permitted. Largest barrier gap is 1.66 points, below the 8-point attention threshold; no winner is established. The recommended follow-up research has not been conducted. This study contains no randomised concept exposure, price test, observed purchase, revenue or longitudinal retention evidence.

beats.headline_intent: Start with flexible meal help, incorporating use-up and budget tasks
beats.analytical_relationship: Broad task requests establish the shortlist; prespecified external-outcome contrasts identify audiences with relevant reported difficulties without proving intervention effects.

beats.headline_intent: Recruit across overlapping needs and household contexts
beats.analytical_relationship: Joint membership prevents exclusive-persona targeting; children status adds a practical recruitment context while separating statistical evidence from the attention threshold.

beats.headline_intent: Keep support optional and leave delivery format open
beats.analytical_relationship: Polarised digital receptivity qualifies broad task demand, while conditional satisfaction cautions against assuming existing users need a replacement.

beats.headline_intent: Use the pilot to resolve usability, adoption and value questions
beats.analytical_relationship: Closely grouped barriers define design questions; behavioural, longitudinal and controlled evidence is needed to progress from a task shortlist to format selection and commercial claims.

method_notes: Only the supplied study materials and analysis tables were used; no tools, external sources or raw-data analyses were used. analysis_claims contain rounded table transcriptions and explicit arithmetic summaries.

All households and targets are fictional. The 2700-household sample uses eight disproportionate age-by-children quota strata. wt_final standardises to the fixed synthetic profile; weighted N is an equivalent sample count, not UK population size. Results cannot establish real UK prevalence.

Every referenced statistic uses its relevant valid-case denominator. Unknown derived states, DK, refusals and unasked follow-ups are distinct. Some source tables label a prefiltered valid domain as eligible; full eligibility is restored where recoverable. The U1 DK/refusal split cannot be recovered from the supplied summaries and is not invented.

All overall 1–5 item distributions are reported, including current-user satisfaction. Codes 97/98 are excluded from valid distributions. Only A2 would be reversed for the planning-orientation index; its reported item distribution is unreversed. Correlated attitudes are not independent corroboration.

All six required contrasts are reported. Supplied inference uses fixed-weight stratified domain-ratio linearisation across eight strata, retaining all sampled rows with zero influence outside valid domains, with no FPC. Two-sided Holm adjustment applies separately to four needs_external and two household_context tests. The reported normal 95% intervals are unadjusted, not simultaneous.

Kish ESS measures weight dispersion and is not substituted for a variance estimator. Inference is conditional on observed valid cases and the synthetic fixed profile; it does not remove nonresponse bias, selection or causal uncertainty.

The 0.5-day and 8-percentage-point thresholds guide descriptive pilot attention, not economic value. B1–B3 count days in seven, including valid zeroes; they do not count shops, meals, quantities or money.

Valid n below 40 requires suppression; n=40–74 requires a small-base warning; ESS below 50 requires a warning. Older paid-user satisfaction is suppressed. No superiority rankings are inferred from numerical leads, and no commercial impact, conversion or retained usage is established.
